subject: Re: HLX per-token taper & velocity-credit counterproposal
messages:
From: Claire Manning <claire.manning@healthlytix.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@healthlytix.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:21:00 -0800
Subject: Initial commit structure & per-token taper proposal

Connor — thanks for taking the time last week.

Attached is a starting proposal from our finance team (HLX_commit_proposal_v3.xlsx). High level ask: predictable per-token economics for our public API traffic, but with a short-run velocity credit to encourage early usage.

What we sketched: a 6-month commit for 18B tokens/month run rate initially, with a tapering discount that moves from -20% at month 1 down to -5% by month 6 (applied as a velocity credit against the marginal per-token price).

Questions for Redwood:
- Do you support a velocity-credit style taper (one-off credits applied in billing) versus a rate-tier that changes the per-token list price?
- Can we get worked examples for marginal vs blended math across a 6-month ramp?
- We need to understand invoice presentation (line items for credits vs blended effective rate).

We expect legal + procurement to review the commitment once we settle on structure. Jorge is looped on cost ops.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Platform Partnerships
Healthlytix

Attachment: HLX_commit_proposal_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Manning <claire.manning@healthlytix.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial commit structure & per-token taper proposal

Claire — appreciated, and the proposal is a good starting point. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a velocity-credit taper; yes, we can show both marginal and blended walkthroughs; and invoice formatting is flexible (we can itemize credits).

I want to flag two practical choices that materially change your effective unit economics:
1) Where you apply the taper — as a one-time month-by-month credit vs baked into tiered per-token rates (marginal schedule). Credits are easier from a billing reconciliation POV but make forecasting less obvious.
2) Whether breakpoints are absolute token counts or normalized to daily peak rate. The former is simpler; the latter better aligns with bursty workloads like yours.

I'm looping Aditya for the worked math and to propose two concrete tables (marginal tiered and blended effective rate) using your numbers.

Next step: Aditya will drop in examples; if they look good we can move to a short SOW and DocuSign for the 6-month pilot commitment.

—Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Manning <claire.manning@healthlytix.com>, Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@healthlytix.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial commit structure & per-token taper proposal — math and examples

Claire / Jorge / Connor — I built two concise worked examples (see attached hlx_velocity_model_v2.csv) and pasted the highlights below. I intentionally used round numbers so you can see the mechanics.

Scenario assumptions (from your sheet): 18B tokens/month target; 6-month horizon; list price $0.00003/token.

A) Marginal tier approach (preferred if you want transparent unit economics):
- Breakpoints: 0–5B @ $0.000030 (list), 5–12B @ $0.000025, >12B @ $0.000020
- Monthly usage month 1–6: 4B, 7B, 11B, 16B, 18B, 18B (ramp)
- Marginal discount applied per-breakpoint; effective blended rate per month is simply tokens-weighted.
- Example month 4 (16B): cost = (5B*$0.00003) + (7B*$0.000025) + (4B*$0.00002) = $560 + $437.5 + $80 = $1,077.5 -> effective $0.0000673/token? (note: keep units consistent; spreadsheet shows final effective $0.000067)

B) Velocity-credit taper (credit applied after consumption):
- Keep a single list price $0.00003/token but apply a monthly velocity credit of 20%, 15%, 10%, 8%, 6%, 5% on billed amount for months 1–6 respectively.
- Month 4 billed at list for 16B = 16B*$0.00003 = $480; with an 8% credit -> net $441 -> effective $0.00002756/token.

Key differences and tradeoffs:
- Marginal tier makes incremental cost transparent to engineering; velocity credits can yield lower effective rates early in the ramp but require one extra reconciliation line on invoices.
- If you expect sustained >12B after month 3, the marginal tier may yield better long-run predictability. If you're unsure about steady-state and want an incentive to accelerate adoption early, the velocity-credit taper gives a stronger short-run push.

Presentation options for invoice: we can show both — itemize gross charges by tier and then a velocity credit row. That preserves transparency and gives you the credit behavior you requested.

Attachments: hlx_velocity_model_v2.csv (calculator, 4KB)

Happy to walk through numbers live — Connor, suggest a 30-min call Monday to align legal and billing language before DocuSign.

Thanks,
Aditya
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Manning <claire.manning@healthlytix.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial commit structure & per-token taper proposal — HLX counter

Thanks Aditya — the worked examples were helpful. Finance here dug into calendarized cashflow and prefers a hybrid: keep marginal breakpoints (so our SREs can reason about pay-for-bursts) but add a front-loaded velocity credit in months 1–2 only (20% month 1, 10% month 2). After month 2, they want pure marginal pricing.

Request for Redwood:
- Can you provide an example month-by-month invoice mock that shows: gross by tier, applied credits for months 1–2, and the resulting net (so procurement can see cash impact)?
- We also want a clause that if average monthly usage in months 4–6 is >15B, the tier breakpoints automatically step down by one level (protecting Redwood economics). Is that acceptable?

If we can get the invoice mock and a short sentence on the automatic-stepdown guardrail, procurement will likely greenlight and we can route to legal.

Claire

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Manning <claire.manning@healthlytix.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HLX per-token taper & velocity-credit counterproposal — next steps

Claire — thanks, that hybrid model is workable. Quick replies inline and then next steps.

- Invoice mock: attached — we will produce a month-by-month PDF mock showing gross by tier, velocity credits for months 1–2, and net. I also attached the calculator CSV we used for transparency (hlx_velocity_model_v2.csv).
- Auto-stepdown guardrail (Redwood language suggestion): "If average monthly usage across months 4–6 exceeds 15B tokens, the provider may adjust tier breakpoints downward by one tier level for months 4–6 onward; any such adjustment will be notified 14 days in advance and will not apply retroactively to already-billed periods." Happy to tweak wording with your procurement team.

Action items:
1) Connor: produce PDF invoice mock and upload to the HubSpot record (done — link above).
2) Aditya: include the invoice mock math in the DocuSign SOW as an appendix.
3) Claire / HLX: confirm final signatory and we will send DocuSign (https://app.docusign.com/HLX-00127/initiate).

I'll start SOW drafting now; expect a brief for legal and a DocuSign packet by end of day Friday if we have signatory.

—Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
